anomalies.obs: On SkylabModule (sheet /SkylabModule/, page 1/4) the net on U7 pin 44, whose symbol function text reads 'HW_RESET', is NET0040 — the same global label that on U11 (BBQ10KBD) pin 6 is ROW1. The physical reset slide switch S2 (sheet /EthernetAndPower/, page 4/4) pin 1 is wired to NET0015, which lands on U7 pin 47 (symbol text 'I2C_CLK'), not on the HW_RESET pin.
anomalies.exp: The specification states S1 is wired as the HW_RESET switch: 'S1 ... pin1→GND, pin2→HW_RESET (SKW92A pin 45)'. The module's HW_RESET input must be a dedicated net tied to the switch, and must not be shared with a keyboard-matrix row.

evidence.quote: SkylabModule page 1/4: U7 pin 44 'HW_RESET' → NET0040; U11 pin 6 'ROW1' → NET0040; U7 pin 47 'I2C_CLK' → NET0015; EthernetAndPower page 4/4: S2 pin 1 → NET0015
S1 ... is, per the netlist, wired as a reset button (S1.1→GND, S1.2→HW_RESET→SKW92A pin 45 HW_RESET)

anomalies.impact: The module's hardware-reset pin is driven by the keyboard scan matrix, so scanning ROW1 will glitch or hold the SoC in reset (board may fail to boot); meanwhile the slide switch toggles an I2C clock line and cannot reset the device.

anomalies.obs: On SkylabModule page 1/4 the gate of the P-channel display-power switch Q3 (NTR2101P) is pulled up to +3V3 by R1 (10 k) and tied to U7 pin 31; the net at that node is NET0022, which is also the label on U11 pin 23 (LEDK_2_3, a keyboard backlight LED cathode).
anomalies.exp: The specification assigns SKW92A pin 31 exclusively as the GPIO that drives the high-side EPD power switch ('U5.31 ... repurposed here as a general output' for Q2's gate). A high-side power-switch gate must not share a net with a matrix-scanned LED line.

evidence.quote: SkylabModule page 1/4: R1 10k between +3V3 and Q3 pin 1; Q3 pin 1 / U7 pin 31 / U11 pin 23 (LEDK_2_3) all carry NET0022
U5.31 (SKW92A GPIO ... repurposed here as a general output). Q2.2 (source) ties to +3V3; Q2.3 (drain) ties to the Display_Power_Switch net

anomalies.impact: Operating the keyboard backlight toggles the e-paper display's power rail (and the 10 k gate pull-up fights the LED driver), causing unintended display power cycling and unreliable backlight control.
